reason: Add the measured GPIO4 bit-1 (AHB 'request') MCU-output->fabric-input entry corridor as two new chipdb datasets: mcu_gpio4_request_paths.csv (BufMUX10 boundary + the one novel X11Y4_RMUX81 fabric bridge) and mcu_gpio4_request_pip_cfg.csv (their exact codewords: InputMUX10 default-input, CFG_RMUX13 set 33;39). Harvested from the vendor route of the gpio4 mine build (tools/agamemnon/harvest_gpio4_request.py); the bridge codeword is triangulated against four ahbrwide corpus builds in sel_dataset.csv. The corridor is loaded only under the new opt-in flag AGAMEMNON_MCU_GPIO4_REQUEST_PATHS (default off), so the default device graph is byte-unchanged and Rule 2 rebuilds the entire retained qualified corpus byte-identical (zero blast radius). Fixes the open BRAM-collision witness handshake root cause: request_async was bound to a generic MCU0.DIN at X10Y5 carrying no GPIO register (docs/GPIO4_REQUEST_CORRIDOR_PROGRESS_20260912.md, memory ag32-bram-open-write-handshake-binding-rootcause-2026-09-12). Opt-in and silicon-unproven until an attended board witness.
